properties.description:
TORDTX

The National Weather Service in Detroit/Pontiac has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Western Saginaw County in southeastern Michigan...
Southeastern Midland County in southeastern Michigan...

* Until 230 PM EDT.

* At 148 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located near Breckenridge, or 11 miles east of Alma, moving
southeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed.
Damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree
damage is likely.

* This dangerous storm will be near...
Merrill around 155 PM EDT.
St. Charles around 200 PM EDT.

Other locations impacted by this tornadic thunderstorm include Brant,
Nelson, Swan Creek, Shiawassee National Wildlife Refuge, Garfield,
Hemlock, Porter Township, and Shields.
properties.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

next few hours. If heavy rain moves back into this region, a
Flash Flood Warning will likely be issued.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Livingston, Corrigan, Goodrich, Seven Oaks, West Livingston, Lake
Livingston State Park, Leggett and Moscow.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
FFWLCH

The National Weather Service in Lake Charles has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern Tyler County in southeastern Texas...

* Until 200 PM CDT.

* At 1055 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches per hour.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Woodville, Warren, Ivanhoe and Hillister.
